swayable.summary: The video explains the difference between closed and open primaries, describing who can vote in each type and how party affiliation affects ballot access. It delivers this information as a straightforward narrated explanation with no personal stories, emotional appeals, or calls to action.
swayable.title: Closed vs. Open Primaries: What Every Voter Should Know

traits.change: Have the messenger introduce themselves as a veteran, for example: 'As a veteran who has voted in both closed and open primaries, I want to explain how these systems work.'

traits.quote: In closed primaries, you can only vote for candidates from your own political party... In open primaries, all voters can choose which ballot to participate in.
traits.change: To drop the contrast, remove the closed-primary section and only describe open primaries without comparing them to closed ones.
The script alone cannot show production value; to signal it, add a line like 'Watch our full animated breakdown at PAX2.org' to imply polished supporting visuals.
Add a line like 'Whether you are a factory worker, a teacher, or a retiree, open primaries make sure your voice counts just like everyone else's.'
Have the messenger introduce themselves as an elected official, for example: 'I am a state representative, and I want to explain how primaries work.'
Add a line like 'I once showed up to vote in a primary and was turned away because I was not registered with the right party — that is what a closed primary does.'
Add a closing line like 'Vote yes on Measure 12 to bring open primaries to our state.'

Replace the closing line 'This gives voters the greatest choice and gives everyone a chance to participate in the vote' with 'Open primaries are an exciting step forward — every voter finally gets a real say!'

traits.quote: In closed primaries, you can only vote for candidates from your own political party.
traits.change: To drop the fact-explaining, remove the definitions of closed and open primaries and replace them with a personal opinion or story instead.
Add a line like 'A voter in our state said: I felt shut out under the closed primary system — my party did not represent me and I had no other option.'

Replace 'This gives voters the greatest choice and gives everyone a chance to participate in the vote' with 'Open primaries are something we can all be proud of — a system that trusts every citizen to make their own choice.'
Add a line like 'Most voters do not know that in some states, independents make up the largest voting bloc yet are completely locked out of closed primaries.'
Add a light line like 'Yes, a registered Republican really can vote on the Green Party ballot — no, the sky will not fall.'
Have the messenger introduce themselves as a well-known public figure, for example: 'Hi, I am [Name], and as someone you may recognize from film, I want to talk about open primaries.'
Add a line like 'It is simply wrong that millions of voters are blocked from participating just because they refuse to join a political party.'

traits.quote: The Constitution says almost nothing about primaries, so the rules for conducting this first stage of voting vary significantly depending on the state and type of election.
traits.change: To sound less scripted, replace that opening with a conversational line like 'So, primaries — you have probably heard the word, but did you know the rules are totally different depending on where you live?'
Add a line like 'A voter in our state said: For the first time I felt like my vote actually mattered, because open primaries let me choose the best candidate, not just the one from my party.'

traits.quote: In open primaries, all voters can choose which ballot to participate in, regardless of party affiliation.
traits.change: To remove the policy facts, cut the descriptions of how closed and open primaries work and replace them with a general opinion about voter participation instead.

traits.quote: This gives voters the greatest choice and gives everyone a chance to participate in the vote.
traits.change: To drop the positive tone, cut that closing line and end instead with a neutral statement like 'These are the two systems currently used across the country.'
Add a line like 'Closed primaries shut out millions of independent voters and hand control of elections to party insiders.'
The script cannot show visual style, but to signal an amateur feel, add a line like 'I am just recording this on my phone because I think this information matters and everyone should hear it.'
Add a line like 'According to the National Conference of State Legislatures, more than a dozen states currently use open primary systems.'
The script cannot show on-screen text, but to signal it, add a direction like 'See the definition on screen now: an open primary lets any registered voter choose any party ballot.'

Have the messenger introduce themselves as an ordinary citizen, for example: 'Hi, I am just a regular voter from this state, and I want to explain what open primaries actually mean for people like us.'
Replace the neutral closing line with 'Open primaries are the fairer system, and every state should adopt them so that no voter is ever left out.'
Add a line like 'Too many people have gone to the polls only to find out they have no real voice in choosing their candidates — that is a quiet failure of our democracy.'
Add a line like 'If we do not open up our primaries, we risk handing all the power to a small group of party insiders who decide elections before most voters ever get a say.'
The script cannot show visual style, but to signal animation, add a line like 'Watch the animated chart now to see exactly how your ballot changes under each system.'
